text_blocks.snippet: The global inflation rate is currently trending downward after reaching a high in 2022. While specific figures vary depending on the source and methodology, it's generally expected to continue to decline through 2025.
snippet_highlighted_words: The global inflation rate is currently trending downward after reaching a high in 2022

list.title: Peak in 2022:
list.snippet: Global inflation surged in 2022, reaching almost 9%, driven by factors like the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine war, according to Statista.

list.title: Declining Trend:
list.snippet: Forecasts indicate a steady decrease in global inflation, with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projecting it to fall from 6.8% in 2023 to 5.9% in 2024 and 4.5% in 2025, according to the IMF.

list.title: Regional Differences:
list.snippet: Inflation rates vary across regions, with some areas experiencing faster disinflation than others.

list.title: Central Bank Actions:
list.snippet: Central banks worldwide have been raising interest rates to combat inflation, which is expected to contribute to the overall decline.

list.title: Factors Influencing Decline:
list.snippet: The decline is expected to be influenced by a combination of factors, including the normalization of supply chains, easing of energy prices, and the impact of monetary policy tightening.

list.title: Core Inflation:
list.snippet: Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, is generally projected to decline more gradually, according to the IMF.

list.title: Data Sources:
list.snippet: Various organizations like the World Bank, IMF, and Statista track and forecast global inflation rates.
